summary.text: A foreword recounting the history of global efforts to validate elimination of mother-to-child transmission of HIV and syphilis since 2014, including Cuba's validation in 2015. It stresses human rights and the involvement of women living with HIV or HBV in services.

sections.extract: The global community has committed to eliminating mother-to-child transmission (EMTCT), also known as vertical transmission, of HIV and syphilis as a public health priority. In 2014 the World Health Organization (WHO) released the first edition of the Global guidance on criteria and processes for validation: elimination of mother-to-child transmission of HIV and syphilis. sections.extract: Foreword This third version of the EMTCT global validation guidance document provides standardized processes and consensus-developed criteria to validate EMTCT of HIV, syphilis and HBV and to recognize high burden countries that have made significant progress on the Path to Elimination. The guidance strongly emphasizes country-led accountability, rigorous analysis, intensive programme assessment and multilevel

It describes the assessment tool's markers and its three guiding questions on human rights, gender equality and meaningful engagement of affected women.

sections.extract: 4.4.2. summary.text: Explains that many sub-Saharan African countries cannot reach validation thresholds because high maternal HIV or syphilis prevalence keeps child case rates high even with low transmission rates. It opens the chapter on the path to elimination and lists the prevalence levels that make a country eligible to apply.

sections.extract: Most countries in sub-Saharan Africa have reported a maternal HIV seroprevalence of >2% and a maternal syphilis seroprevalence of >1%. Many countries in East and Southern Africa have maternal HIV prevalence of >15%, with some as high as 25%. Even if the MTCT rate of <5% is reached, high HIV burden countries have been unable to achieve EMTCT validation due to their elevated HIV prevalence among pregnant women, which

summary.text: States that countries seeking certification on the path to elimination follow the same procedure as for validation. It begins a table of prevalence requirements, impact indicators and programme targets for each tier, with the bronze-tier targets for HIV, syphilis and hepatitis B.

sections.extract: 5. Path to elimination: recognizing progress towards EMTCT in countries with a high burden of HIV, syphilis and HBV A country seeking certification on the PTE for HIV and syphilis follows the same procedure as a country requesting validation of EMTCT. sections.extract: 6.1. Special populations Most countries face challenges with delivery of health care services to members of key and vulnerable populations (including migrants, the internally displaced, immigrants, non-citizen residents, indigenous/aboriginal/First Nation people, members of other mobile populations and adolescent girls and young women). summary.text: Specifies infant HIV testing at 6–8 weeks and 18 months, or three months after breastfeeding ends, so that all infections are captured, including in non-breastfeeding settings. It introduces special considerations for small countries and island states, whose data should be verified by regional structures during country missions.

sections.extract: 42 Criteria and processes for validation: EMTCT of HIV, Syphilis and Hepatitis B virus The national validation report should provide testing data for infants and HIV-exposed children at 6–8 weeks of age and at the end of 18 months (or three months after the end of breastfeeding, if longer than 18 months). This schedule should ensure that all possible cases of infants and young children who acquire HIV are captured

summary.text: Opens the chapter on the validation process, emphasizing a public health approach that strengthens health systems while upholding rights, participation and gender equality. It advises countries to confirm they meet minimum criteria before applying and describes the national, regional and global teams that verify country reports using standard assessment tools.

sections.extract: Achieving EMTCT of HIV, syphilis and HBV requires a public health approach based on strengthening the health system to provide the maximum health benefit within the available resources while realizing rights to health, participation and gender equality. The validation approach sets the standards for quality and accessible interventions and services, with a focus on integration, person-centred care and community
